1	# Design
2	
3	<!-- Ported from the 2026-09-25 shared OpenSpec session in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_).
4	     Revised 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 for the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: local MCP, Option A2. -->
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	See proposal.md for motivation and the four capability specs for the behavior contract. This design follows the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: a local MCP, and Option A2 for agent identity (see Decision 4). It depends on the `mcp-session-access` handoff specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff`, which is not yet in this repository.
9	
10	The checkout has useful pieces, but no implemented agent-grant layer was found:
11	
12	- Both client admin panels create a 45-second handoff through `create_secret_token` and open `/auth/token` with `/auth/group` as the destination. The website establishes a cookie session. `secret_tokens.sql` supports one-time consumption.
13	- `Concept` represents node instances, schemas, and materialized relationships. `Content` joins by `(space_id, source_local_id)` and has multiple variants. The `my_*` views and access helpers already express space and resource-level readability.
14	- `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimensional `text-embedding-3-small` vectors and ranks by cosine distance. Its existing general search RPC has a relevance threshold and no discourse-type predicate. The Roam search experiment subsequently looks up titles and filters locally; that cannot serve headless retrieval.
15	- Obsidian embeds `direct` title content. Roam also embeds `direct_and_description` for some nodes. Preserve these existing vectors and inputs, as agreed; no title-only re-embedding migration is required.
16	- Full content is synced separately. Roam converts it into a cross-app representation; Obsidian stores markdown. Missing full content and missing embeddings are distinct states.
17	- `apps/website/app/api/embeddings/openai/small/route.ts` embeds text with the team's OpenAI key. It has no authentication: it applies CORS only, which non-browser callers ignore.
18	- On `origin/main` (2026-11-11), ENG-1985 added `dbNodeToCrossApp` and `dbNodesToCrossApp`, and ENG-2091 made discovery return `DbCrossAppNode` in a `SharedNodeListing`. The other facts in this list were read from an older checkout of `main`.
19	- Most row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role; four target `authenticated`. No custom access token hook is configured (it is commented out in `packages/database/supabase/config.toml`).
20	
21	## Goals / Non-Goals
22	
23	**Goals:** Reuse existing data, vectors, and access semantics; expose only read operations to agents; keep the MCP and the direct API on the same retrieval semantics; expose sync gaps without silently substituting incomplete content.
24	
25	**Non-Goals:** A new personal identity system, copied permission snapshots, a second embedding pipeline, hybrid ranking, attachment/storage APIs, or a general-purpose database proxy. A separate agent principal (Option B) and a hosted MCP are out of v0. The database package owns SQL/contracts; the website owns the API routes and the local MCP owns its transport.
26	
27	## Decisions
28	
29	### 1. A local MCP that calls the database directly
30	
31	The MCP is a local stdio server that the user installs and the agent client launches on the user's machine. It connects to Supabase with the handed-over space account session and calls the narrow retrieval RPCs directly. No DG-hosted layer sits between the MCP and the database, and no DG-hosted MCP endpoint exists in v0.
32	
33	```
34	Roam / Obsidian --> connect command --> session bundle (shown once)
35	                                               |
36	                                 local MCP config on the user's machine
37	                                               |
38	agent client --stdio--> local MCP --+--> Supabase retrieval RPCs (as the space account)
39	                                    |
40	                                    +--> website embedding route (search queries only)
41	
42	developer --HTTPS + bearer token--> apps/website API routes --> same retrieval RPCs
43	```
44	
45	The retrieval RPCs are the shared core. Each MCP tool validates its inputs, calls one RPC, and returns structured results plus a compact text representation. All tools are marked read-only.
46	
47	The RPCs are a contract with every installed copy of the MCP, and those copies cannot be force-updated. Change an RPC's signature only by adding a new version alongside the old one.
48	
49	**Direct API.** A developer-facing API for callers not using MCP is a set of thin routes in `apps/website` (`headless-retrieval-api`). Each route authenticates the caller's bearer access token against Supabase, embeds search queries on the server, and calls the same retrieval RPCs as the space account, so row-level security applies. The routes hold no credential between requests. The MCP does not depend on them.
50	
51	**Alternative for the API:** documenting the retrieval RPCs themselves as the API needs no hosting, but makes the database schema a public contract, returns raw Postgres errors, and leaves callers to embed queries through the unauthenticated route.
52	
53	**Alternatives:** A hosted remote MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 design) reaches ChatGPT and needs no install, but requires a hosted credential transport. It was rejected on 2026-11-10 in favour of a local MCP, given the constraint to write to the platform later and target users who already work in agentic harnesses. Routing the local MCP through a hosted API was also considered: it would absorb RPC changes, but adds no security, because the database already refuses writes made with the MCP's session (Decision 4).
54	
55	### 2. Hand the MCP its own space account session
56	
57	The credential is a Supabase session for the space account, opened by the plugin and handed over as a bundle: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID, and refresh token. `mcp-session-access` specifies the handoff, the session registry, and sign-out. The plugin keeps no copy and shows the bundle once. The MCP persists each rotated refresh token and runs as a single instance per bundle. The session's registry row is what makes it read-only (Decision 4).
58	
59	**Alternative (superseded 2026-11-10):** The 2026-09-25 design provisioned a separate Supabase auth user per agent grant, issued an opaque final credential through a website management session, and stored the agent's login secret server-side. That needs a hosted server and a separate principal, and A2 has neither.
60	
61	### 3. ~~Proposed MCP connection uses a credential-bearing URL~~ — removed
62	
63	Removed 2026-11-10. It existed to carry a credential to a hosted MCP through clients that cannot send custom headers. A local MCP reads the bundle from its own configuration. The client/redaction release gate and the OAuth alternative are removed with it.
64	
65	### 4. The database enforces read-only on handed-over sessions (Option A2)
66	
67	Decided 2026-11-10: the MCP acts as the space account, and the database refuses writes made with its session. `mcp-session-access` records each handed-over session in `mcp_session`. A Supabase custom access token hook runs whenever a token is issued or refreshed. When the token's session is in `mcp_session`, the hook sets the JWT `role` claim to a read-only database role, `mcp_reader` (name proposed), instead of `authenticated`. Plugin sessions keep `authenticated`.
68	
69	`mcp_reader` has `SELECT` on the tables retrieval reads, and `EXECUTE` on the retrieval RPCs and the access helpers they call. It has no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, and no `EXECUTE` on sync, upsert or `create_secret_token`. Row-level security still applies: policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, and the four `TO authenticated` policies need review. Reads therefore follow the space account's current access with no grant layer.
70	
71	The MCP's tools and the API's operations still expose only retrieval, but they are no longer what enforces read-only.
72	
73	**Revocation is delayed.** The hook runs at issue and refresh, so a signed-out session keeps its current access token until `jwt_expiry` (3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this over B's immediate revocation.
74	
75	**Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product notes record "option A2" (Roam block `guIcK3Z9M`) and name the threat as overeager agentic harnesses that bypass the MCP's guards. A tool-layer gate is that kind of guard; a database role is not. The spec owner chose plain A on 2026-11-12, then adopted A2 on 2026-11-13 after checking the meeting recording.
76	
77	**Alternatives:** (A) the same session with the space account's full permissions and read-only only at the tool layer. It is about a week less work, but any process holding the bundle can write to the space. (B) a separate, permanently read-only agent principal with an `agent_reader` role and a grant table, the 2026-09-25 version of this decision. It revokes immediately, but the 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for about twice A2's extra work.
78	
79	### 5. Represent nodes as CrossApp nodes
80	
81	**Changed 2026-11-13: the node identifier is now the node's `rid`, not `Concept.id`, to match Sid's `shared-node-discovery` spec ([PR #1570](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1570)), in which discovery returns each node as a `CrossAppNode`.** ENG-1985 and ENG-2091 implemented that on 2026-11-11: `dbNodesToCrossApp` in `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts database rows to `DbCrossAppNode` (a `CrossAppNode` with `rid` and `modifiedAt` required), and discovery returns a `SharedNodeListing` of `{ nodes, spaces }`. Retrieval uses the same converter, so an agent and the plugins see the same node under the same ID.
82	
83	**IDs.** A node's ID is its `rid`: its space's URI followed by its `localId` (a Roam block uid, an Obsidian file's ID). A type's ID is the node's `nodeType`: the type's `localId` within the node's space, or the type's `rid` when it belongs to another space. Identically named types in different spaces stay separate. Look a node up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
84	
85	**Payload.** Return each node as a `DbCrossAppNode`, inside an envelope that follows discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` pattern: the spaces map gives each node's space name, URI and platform, and type labels come from `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`. Search adds a score and an excerpt per node. Do not define a separate node type for agents.
86	
87	**Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`; `coreTitle` is the title without the type's format. The converter leaves out `content.full`, as discovery does, so get-node fetches the full Content separately, as node import does, and returns stored text/markdown, not rendered HTML. Preserve source links as text; do not fetch referenced assets or mint storage download URLs. Provenance comes from the `rid` and the spaces map. A source link refers to the origin and never claims the node exists in the caller's vault.
88	
89	**Gaps are errors.** `dbNodesToCrossApp` skips any row it cannot convert (missing direct content, author or node type) and logs a warning. Listings and search may skip such rows, as discovery does. Get-node for one ID must not: it converts the row with `dbNodeToCrossApp` and maps the failure to an explicit code, so a node that doesn't exist or isn't readable returns `not_found` and a node lacking its full Content returns `content_unavailable`. Distinguish a stored empty body from a missing row. Fixture validation must exercise these states for both platforms before release.
90	
91	**Type discovery** derives distinct types from readable node instances, independently of embeddings, with labels from the readable schemas. Missing schema data is a sync/access-integrity error, not a reason to bypass permissions.
92	
93	**Alternatives:** `Concept.id` serialized as a decimal string (the previous version of this decision) is a database-internal ID that no plugin uses; it would give the same node a second identity. An agent-specific node payload would rebuild, from the same rows, the second node representation that ENG-2091 just removed. Content IDs as node IDs would expose content variants as duplicate nodes.
94	
95	### 6. Reuse semantic vectors with a retrieval-specific query
96	
97	Embed each search query with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions to match the existing table. A local MCP has no server and no provider key, so it embeds through the existing website route `/api/embeddings/openai/small` and passes the vector to the search RPC. That route is unauthenticated today; see Risks. The API's search route embeds on the server after authenticating the caller. A caller-supplied vector cannot widen access, because the RPC ranks only nodes readable by the caller.
98	
99	Add a dedicated read-only search RPC using the existing embedding table and cosine-distance ordering. Keep existing RPC behavior for current consumers. In this query:
100	
101	- Resolve readable discourse node instances and any selected schema IDs.
102	- Join their current non-obsolete, usable embeddings for existing `direct` and `direct_and_description` content. Preserve the stored input semantics, including descriptions.
103	- Where multiple eligible embeddings represent one node, use its best similarity and return it once.
104	- Sort by similarity descending and node ID as a stable tie-breaker, then apply the requested limit. Authorization, type filtering, and deduplication occur before the limit.
105	
106	Do not copy the current threshold predicate or the Roam experiment's post-limit local filtering. Do not replace the threshold with zero, since negative similarities remain eligible. Do not add keyword indexes, hybrid fusion, or collection re-embedding.
107	
108	Nodes without a current usable embedding are absent from search but remain eligible for get-node/type discovery/context. Embedding-provider failures are errors, not empty results. Create excerpts from the first 300 Unicode code points of available synced body text, with a fallback to the stored semantic input when full content is absent; excerpts are not evidence that the query matched the body. Both interfaces document this behavior.
109	
110	**Alternative:** Calling the existing threshold RPC unchanged violates the agreed no-cutoff behavior and can lose results when type filtering follows its limit. A dedicated query reuses the existing search mechanism while preserving current consumers.
111	
112	### 7. Resolve discourse context using named roles
113	
114	Find readable materialized relation instances connected to the requested node, explicitly filtering `is_relation` and excluding schemas. Use `reference_content` source/destination roles to determine direction; the derived `refs` array identifies candidates but does not encode direction and can include other references. Require the relation, relationship type metadata, and both endpoints to be readable before returning a relationship summary.
115	
116	Return each relation ID with its type, direction, and connected-node summary. Preserve separate materialized relationships rather than deduplicating by labels. A self-link can produce both incoming and outgoing entries. Do not traverse beyond the requested node's incident relationships or expand ordinary backlinks.
117	
118	Return complete one-hop results within the host's response budget. If the result cannot fit, return an explicit `result_too_large` error rather than silently truncate or add an undocumented pagination contract. Full node bodies use the same complete-or-error policy. A proposed 1 MiB serialized response budget is an implementation guardrail to validate against Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, not a relevance or latency target.
119	
120	**Alternative:** Expanding every ID in `refs` would expose non-discourse references and lose direction. Silent truncation would make incomplete discourse context appear complete.
121	
122	### 8. API contract and operational behavior
123	
124	Direct API routes and the corresponding MCP tools:
125	
126	| Direct API | MCP tool | Inputs |
127	| --- | --- | --- |
128	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | Node `rid` |
129	| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | Query, optional type IDs, optional limit |
130	| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | None |
131	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | Node `rid` |
132	
133	Node IDs are `rid`s (Decision 5). They contain `/` and `:`, so the API takes them URL-encoded in the path.
134	
135	Use shared Zod input/output schemas and generate or check the tool and API documentation against them. Reject blank queries, malformed `rid`s, empty explicitly supplied type filters, and non-integer/out-of-range limits with `invalid_request`. Omitted limits default to 10; valid limits are 1-30. Unknown but syntactically valid type IDs simply match no nodes. Results carry a request ID and `data` or an error object with a stable code and safe message.
136	
137	Missing, expired, or signed-out sessions fail authentication. Use the same `not_found` for nonexistent and unreadable nodes, `content_unavailable` for a readable node with missing required synced content, and `result_too_large` for response-budget failures; database and embedding failures are dependency errors. Return these as MCP tool errors with the same codes rather than serializing exceptions; the API maps them to 401, 404, 409, 422 and 503. Do not turn failed queries into successful empty collections.
138	
139	Keep diagnostic logs to request ID, operation, duration, result count, and error category. Exclude the bundle, refresh and access tokens, query text, node bodies, and provider payloads. A local MCP's logs stay on the user's machine. The API's redaction covers the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs as well as application logs. No read-history UI or auditing subsystem is added. Documentation includes the install and setup flow, private bundle handling, search coverage/limits, sync-gap errors, and source-link limitations.
140	
141	## Risks / Trade-offs
142	
143	- [Revocation waits for token expiry] → Accepted under A2 (Decision 4). A signed-out session keeps its current access token for up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
144	- [The access token hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup in `mcp_session`, return claims unchanged for other sessions, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook enabled.
145	- [A read grant missing from `mcp_reader` breaks retrieval silently] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows when the role lacks a grant or a `TO authenticated` policy excludes it. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`, not as `authenticated`.
146	- [The bundle reads everything the space can read, from a plain file the agent harness can read] → Agent clients keep MCP configuration in plain files on the user's machine (for example `claude_desktop_config.json`, or `~/.claude.json` for Claude Code). Accepted for v0. Setup documentation states the risk.
147	- [The API carries a bearer token through the website] → An MCP session's token is read-only. A plugin session's token can write, but the API exposes only reads and never stores the token. Redaction covers the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs as well as application logs. A token that leaks stays valid until it expires, up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
148	- [Cutting off one MCP depends on `mcp-session-access` sign-out] → If per-session sign-out is not in v0 (open there as task 0.4), the only cut-off is changing the space password, which signs out every plugin instance of the space.
149	- [The query embedding route is unauthenticated] → MCP search depends on it, and today anyone can spend the team's OpenAI quota through it, independent of this change. API search embeds on the server behind authentication instead. Hardening it is a follow-up, not this change: the shipped Roam and Obsidian plugins call the route without auth during sync and search, and installed copies cannot be force-updated, so a check needs a compatible migration path.
150	- [Installed MCP copies pin the RPC signatures] → Copies on users' machines cannot be force-updated. Add RPC versions alongside old ones rather than changing signatures in place.
151	- [One bundle reads one space] → A user with several spaces needs one MCP entry per space. Whether one agent should span several spaces is an open product question.
152	- [Existing embedding inputs differ across platforms] → Preserve and document that behavior, use deterministic vector fixtures for query correctness, and defer relevance tuning until real-query examples exist.
153	- [Full content, schema metadata, or provenance can be missing] → Return explicit sync/data errors and validate representative Roam and Obsidian fixtures. Do not expand ingestion or attachment scope to conceal gaps.
154	- [Shared nodes surprise users or origin links do not open locally] → Explain that results reflect readable synced data rather than local import membership and label provenance as origin.
155	- [Large bodies/context exceed client budgets] → Validate the response budget and surface a complete-or-error result. Pagination or truncation semantics require a later product decision.
156	
157	## Migration Plan
158	
159	1. Land `mcp-session-access` first: the session registry, the handoff helper, and the plugin connect command. This change depends on it. Then add `mcp_reader` and the access token hook (Decision 4), and enable the hook on the hosted project.
160	2. Add the narrow retrieval RPCs — node fetch, search without a relevance threshold, type discovery, and one-hop context — through the database's declarative schema/migration workflow. Existing clients and search RPCs retain their behavior.
161	3. Build the local MCP with the four tools over those RPCs and the embedding route, and the direct API routes in `apps/website` over the same RPCs.
162	4. Test permission gains/losses, both platform payloads, shared unimported nodes, type filters, negative similarities, missing embeddings/content, inaccessible relation endpoints, and parity between the MCP and the direct API. Assert that the database refuses writes made with a handed-over session and still accepts the plugin's. Install the MCP in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with a test space's bundle, record client versions, and demonstrate all four operations with Roam and Obsidian closed. Run required repository validation before requesting implementation review.
163	5. Release the MCP to a limited validation cohort, then expand only after those checks pass. No bulk content migration or re-embedding is part of rollout.
164	6. Rollback withdraws the MCP package and signs out registered MCP sessions; without per-session sign-out, change the space password. Additive retrieval RPCs can remain unused; do not delete synced nodes, content, vectors, or existing group access.
165	
166	## Open Questions
167	
168	The credential label copy, example queries for documentation, and a future relevance evaluation dataset can be settled during implementation without changing this architecture.
169	
170	### Per-capability open decisions
171	
172	<!-- Held here rather than in the spec deltas: openspec validate warns that a
173	     "## Open decisions" section in a delta is not carried into the main spec on archive. -->
174	
175	- **`agent-read-access`:** The per-space model stands as the v0 baseline after the 2026-11-10 decision. Whether one agent should span several spaces is open.
176	- **`discourse-mcp`:** The client set is Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is out of v0.
177	- **`discourse-retrieval`:** Implementation design for access/type filtering, limits, excerpts, errors, and missing embeddings is above. Real-query relevance examples and numerical quality targets are deferred. Hybrid search is future work.
178	- **`headless-retrieval-api`:** Endpoint paths, response/error conventions, and minimum troubleshooting logs are in Decision 8. No latency target or broader read-auditing capability is committed.

=== agent-read-access/spec.md
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Let a space hand an agent its own session for the space account, so the agent reads the space's synced discourse graph with the space's current access.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Session handoff from the plugin

An agent SHALL obtain its credential through the `mcp-session-access` handoff: a Roam or Obsidian plugin signed in as the space account opens a new session and shows the user a bundle once. No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required.

#### Scenario: Setup from either supported platform

- **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in an authenticated Roam or Obsidian client
- **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new session of that client's space account
- **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged

### Requirement: Per-space principal

The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection and SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts used by the same human. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space.

#### Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes

- **GIVEN** a human uses spaces A and B and a node in B is not readable by A's space account
- **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A
- **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B
- **AND** access through B requires a bundle from space B

#### Scenario: Accessible shared node

- **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing
- **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node
- **THEN** the node is eligible without requiring local import or authorship by the space account

### Requirement: Current permissions and revocation

The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions. Removing access SHALL stop subsequent retrieval of affected data, and adding access SHALL make affected synced data eligible, without a new bundle. Signing out a handed-over session SHALL stop it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds MAY remain valid until they expire.

#### Scenario: Permissions change after handoff

- **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over
- **THEN** subsequent requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B
- **AND** a new bundle is not required

#### Scenario: Session sign-out

- **WHEN** a user signs out a handed-over session
- **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh that session
- **AND** requests fail once its current access token expires

### Requirement: The database enforces read-only on handed-over sessions

The database SHALL refuse any create, modify or delete made with a handed-over session, including calls to sync, upsert and session-management functions, whichever client makes them. The session SHALL keep the space account's read access. The plugin's own sessions SHALL keep their permissions. The MCP SHALL expose only retrieval tools, and the direct API SHALL expose only retrieval operations. Missing, expired or signed-out sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval.

#### Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node

- **GIVEN** the space account can edit a node
- **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify that node
- **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification
- **AND** the node remains unchanged

#### Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools

- **GIVEN** a process holds the handed-over session and the space account can edit a node
- **WHEN** it modifies the node by calling the database directly with that session
- **THEN** the database refuses the modification
- **AND** the node remains unchanged

#### Scenario: Plugin session keeps write access

- **GIVEN** a plugin has handed over a session
- **WHEN** the plugin writes with its own session
- **THEN** the write succeeds

#### Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval

- **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing, expired or signed-out session
- **THEN** no discourse data is returned
=== discourse-mcp/spec.md
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Expose headless discourse retrieval to agent clients through one platform-independent local MCP, run on the user's machine with a space account session handed over by the plugin.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Four retrieval tools

MCP SHALL expose tools for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types, and get-discourse-context. Tool descriptions and input definitions SHALL make the operations and supported search/type-filter inputs discoverable. The tools SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` and `agent-read-access` contracts.

#### Scenario: Tool discovery and invocation

- **WHEN** an authenticated agent client discovers the MCP tools
- **THEN** all four operations and their input definitions are available
- **AND** invoking them applies the agreed payloads, access rules, search limits, and discourse-context boundaries

### Requirement: Direct API and MCP parity

MCP SHALL accept the same handed-over session as the direct API and SHALL expose equivalent retrieval semantics. A caller SHALL NOT gain access to additional data by switching interfaces.

#### Scenario: Equivalent requests through both interfaces

- **GIVEN** unchanged data and permissions and a valid handed-over session
- **WHEN** equivalent requests are made through MCP and the direct API
- **THEN** they apply equivalent eligibility, payload, filtering, ranking, and limit rules

#### Scenario: Signed-out session across interfaces

- **WHEN** a session previously used successfully with both interfaces is signed out
- **THEN** once its current access token expires, subsequent requests through both interfaces are denied

### Requirement: Supported agent clients

V0 SHALL support documented installation and setup of the local MCP, and successful execution of all four operations, in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. ChatGPT is not supported in v0, because it cannot launch a local MCP. This capability SHALL require no separate platform-specific MCP for Roam versus Obsidian.

#### Scenario: Validate each target client

- **GIVEN** synced readable data and a bundle created through the supported handoff
- **WHEN** installation, setup and tool execution are validated independently in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex
- **THEN** each client can launch the MCP and complete all four retrieval operations
- **AND** retrieval works with Roam and Obsidian closed
=== discourse-retrieval/spec.md
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Let agents retrieve synced discourse node text, search by meaning using existing embeddings, discover usable node types, and follow explicit one-hop discourse context within current read access.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the handed-over space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that returned nodes have been imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the principal but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the agent fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not assert local import membership

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** an agent requests a node that its principal cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval does not return the node's content or metadata

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return its ID, title, type, full synced text body, and source/provenance link. The body SHALL reflect stored synced text, without fetching current content from the client application. Attachment downloads and image/file contents SHALL remain outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** an agent fetches a readable synced node containing text and a link to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and full stored text, including source links present in that text
- **AND** the response does not download or embed the attachment's file contents

### Requirement: Existing semantic search <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL reuse the existing semantic search functionality and stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings. Search SHALL NOT require re-embedding the collection as titles only. Matching SHALL reflect the existing embedding inputs rather than promise full-body coverage. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking. Each result SHALL contain node ID, title, type, a short excerpt, and source/provenance link, ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Semantic search results

- **WHEN** an agent submits a query with eligible nodes that have current searchable embeddings
- **THEN** results are ranked by semantic similarity using those embeddings and include the required result fields
- **AND** a node is not excluded solely because its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an existing embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the agent searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking without being replaced by a title-only embedding

#### Scenario: Unembedded body changes

- **GIVEN** stored searchable embeddings, permissions, and filters remain unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** that change does not directly alter its semantic matching score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and return at most 30 results per request. A supported requested limit between 1 and 30 SHALL bound the response. V0 SHALL offer no pagination and SHALL NOT discard eligible searchable nodes solely because their relevance is low. An empty collection SHALL mean there are no eligible searchable nodes under the access and type constraints, not that a relevance threshold was unmet.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the agent searches without a limit or with a supported limit of 20
- **THEN** the respective responses contain 10 or 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes with weak semantic similarity and a requested limit of 10
- **WHEN** the agent searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order without rejection by a relevance cutoff

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes satisfy the principal's access and requested type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result collection

#### Scenario: Requested limit exceeds the maximum

- **WHEN** a request specifies a limit above 30
- **THEN** the service does not return more than 30 results

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL expose type IDs and names only for types present on nodes the principal can currently read, including accessible shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type IDs with OR semantics. Omitting the filter SHALL search across all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is present on a readable shared node and type B occurs only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the agent discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is available and type B is absent

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the agent searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B and is readable by the principal

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the agent searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded based on type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships for a readable node. Each returned relationship SHALL identify its type and direction relative to the requested node and the connected node's ID, title, and type. Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded, and connected bodies SHALL be separately retrievable through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT perform arbitrary-depth traversal.

#### Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the agent requests discourse context for A and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, with the corresponding connected-node summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the ordinary backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B, and C have explicit relationships A to B and B to C, with no A to C relationship
- **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** that call does not traverse B to return C
- **AND** a subsequent request for B's discourse context can retrieve the relationship to C

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Give developers a documented interface for direct discourse retrieval using the same space account session and behavioral contracts as MCP.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Direct access to retrieval operations <!-- roam:9iZVchr-f -->

The system SHALL provide a directly callable API for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types, and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` and `agent-read-access` contracts without requiring an MCP client.

#### Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly

- **WHEN** a developer uses a valid handed-over session to call each of the four API operations
- **THEN** each operation is available directly and applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
- **AND** an MCP connection is not required

### Requirement: Documented developer contract <!-- roam:OlfosIASW -->

The API SHALL document authentication, operation inputs and outputs, errors, search limits, type-filter semantics, and the per-space access model. Documentation SHALL explain that readable unimported nodes can appear, existing embeddings determine semantic coverage, semantic search can return weak matches, and v0 search has no pagination.

#### Scenario: Set up a direct integration

- **WHEN** a developer follows the API documentation using a handed-over session
- **THEN** the documentation supplies callable examples for all four operations and explains how to interpret their results and errors

### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup <!-- roam:UCHDnQtCv -->

After session handoff and data sync, direct retrieval SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian being open. Responses SHALL use the database's synced state rather than require a live connection to either client application.

#### Scenario: Source client is closed

- **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a handed-over session
- **WHEN** the source application is closed and the developer calls the retrieval API
- **THEN** eligible synced data remains retrievable

content.content:
1	# Design
2	
3	<!-- Ported from the 2026-09-25 shared OpenSpec session in Roam (block LPDwCRT6_).
4	     Revised 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 for the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: local MCP, Option A2. -->
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	See proposal.md for motivation and the four capability specs for the behavior contract. This design follows the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product decisions: a local MCP, and Option A2 for agent identity (see Decision 4). It depends on the `mcp-session-access` handoff specified in the Roam page `Spec: MCP token handoff`, which is not yet in this repository.
9	
10	The checkout has useful pieces, but no implemented agent-grant layer was found:
11	
12	- Both client admin panels create a 45-second handoff through `create_secret_token` and open `/auth/token` with `/auth/group` as the destination. The website establishes a cookie session. `secret_tokens.sql` supports one-time consumption.
13	- `Concept` represents node instances, schemas, and materialized relationships. `Content` joins by `(space_id, source_local_id)` and has multiple variants. The `my_*` views and access helpers already express space and resource-level readability.
14	- `embedding.sql` stores 1536-dimensional `text-embedding-3-small` vectors and ranks by cosine distance. Its existing general search RPC has a relevance threshold and no discourse-type predicate. The Roam search experiment subsequently looks up titles and filters locally; that cannot serve headless retrieval.
15	- Obsidian embeds `direct` title content. Roam also embeds `direct_and_description` for some nodes. Preserve these existing vectors and inputs, as agreed; no title-only re-embedding migration is required.
16	- Full content is synced separately. Roam converts it into a cross-app representation; Obsidian stores markdown. Missing full content and missing embeddings are distinct states.
17	- `apps/website/app/api/embeddings/openai/small/route.ts` embeds text with the team's OpenAI key. It has no authentication: it applies CORS only, which non-browser callers ignore.
18	- On `origin/main` (2026-11-11), ENG-1985 added `dbNodeToCrossApp` and `dbNodesToCrossApp`, and ENG-2091 made discovery return `DbCrossAppNode` in a `SharedNodeListing`. The other facts in this list were read from an older checkout of `main`.
19	- Most row-level security policies have no `TO` clause, so they apply to every database role; four target `authenticated`. No custom access token hook is configured (it is commented out in `packages/database/supabase/config.toml`).
20	
21	## Goals / Non-Goals
22	
23	**Goals:** Reuse existing data, vectors, and access semantics; expose only read operations to agents; keep the MCP and the direct API on the same retrieval semantics; expose sync gaps without silently substituting incomplete content.
24	
25	**Non-Goals:** A new personal identity system, copied permission snapshots, a second embedding pipeline, hybrid ranking, attachment/storage APIs, or a general-purpose database proxy. A separate agent principal (Option B) and a hosted MCP are out of v0. The database package owns SQL/contracts; the website owns the API routes and the local MCP owns its transport.
26	
27	## Decisions
28	
29	### 1. A local MCP that calls the database directly
30	
31	The MCP is a local stdio server that the user installs and the agent client launches on the user's machine. It connects to Supabase with the handed-over space account session and calls the narrow retrieval RPCs directly. No DG-hosted layer sits between the MCP and the database, and no DG-hosted MCP endpoint exists in v0.
32	
33	```
34	Roam / Obsidian --> connect command --> session bundle (shown once)
35	                                               |
36	                                 local MCP config on the user's machine
37	                                               |
38	agent client --stdio--> local MCP --+--> Supabase retrieval RPCs (as the space account)
39	                                    |
40	                                    +--> website embedding route (search queries only)
41	
42	developer --HTTPS + bearer token--> apps/website API routes --> same retrieval RPCs
43	```
44	
45	The retrieval RPCs are the shared core. Each MCP tool validates its inputs, calls one RPC, and returns structured results plus a compact text representation. All tools are marked read-only.
46	
47	The RPCs are a contract with every installed copy of the MCP, and those copies cannot be force-updated. Change an RPC's signature only by adding a new version alongside the old one.
48	
49	**Direct API.** A developer-facing API for callers not using MCP is a set of thin routes in `apps/website` (`headless-retrieval-api`). Each route authenticates the caller's bearer access token against Supabase, embeds search queries on the server, and calls the same retrieval RPCs as the space account, so row-level security applies. The routes hold no credential between requests. The MCP does not depend on them.
50	
51	**Alternative for the API:** documenting the retrieval RPCs themselves as the API needs no hosting, but makes the database schema a public contract, returns raw Postgres errors, and leaves callers to embed queries through the unauthenticated route.
52	
53	**Alternatives:** A hosted remote MCP in `apps/website` (the 2026-09-25 design) reaches ChatGPT and needs no install, but requires a hosted credential transport. It was rejected on 2026-11-10 in favour of a local MCP, given the constraint to write to the platform later and target users who already work in agentic harnesses. Routing the local MCP through a hosted API was also considered: it would absorb RPC changes, but adds no security, because the database already refuses writes made with the MCP's session (Decision 4).
54	
55	### 2. Hand the MCP its own space account session
56	
57	The credential is a Supabase session for the space account, opened by the plugin and handed over as a bundle: Supabase URL, anon key, space ID, and refresh token. `mcp-session-access` specifies the handoff, the session registry, and sign-out. The plugin keeps no copy and shows the bundle once. The MCP persists each rotated refresh token and runs as a single instance per bundle. The session's registry row is what makes it read-only (Decision 4).
58	
59	**Alternative (superseded 2026-11-10):** The 2026-09-25 design provisioned a separate Supabase auth user per agent grant, issued an opaque final credential through a website management session, and stored the agent's login secret server-side. That needs a hosted server and a separate principal, and A2 has neither.
60	
61	### 3. ~~Proposed MCP connection uses a credential-bearing URL~~ — removed
62	
63	Removed 2026-11-10. It existed to carry a credential to a hosted MCP through clients that cannot send custom headers. A local MCP reads the bundle from its own configuration. The client/redaction release gate and the OAuth alternative are removed with it.
64	
65	### 4. The database enforces read-only on handed-over sessions (Option A2)
66	
67	Decided 2026-11-10: the MCP acts as the space account, and the database refuses writes made with its session. `mcp-session-access` records each handed-over session in `mcp_session`. A Supabase custom access token hook runs whenever a token is issued or refreshed. When the token's session is in `mcp_session`, the hook sets the JWT `role` claim to a read-only database role, `mcp_reader` (name proposed), instead of `authenticated`. Plugin sessions keep `authenticated`.
68	
69	`mcp_reader` has `SELECT` on the tables retrieval reads, and `EXECUTE` on the retrieval RPCs and the access helpers they call. It has no `INSERT`, `UPDATE` or `DELETE`, and no `EXECUTE` on sync, upsert or `create_secret_token`. Row-level security still applies: policies without a `TO` clause cover `mcp_reader`, and the four `TO authenticated` policies need review. Reads therefore follow the space account's current access with no grant layer.
70	
71	The MCP's tools and the API's operations still expose only retrieval, but they are no longer what enforces read-only.
72	
73	**Revocation is delayed.** The hook runs at issue and refresh, so a signed-out session keeps its current access token until `jwt_expiry` (3600 s). The 2026-11-10 meeting accepted this over B's immediate revocation.
74	
75	**Decision record:** the 2026-11-10 Sync / Protocol Product notes record "option A2" (Roam block `guIcK3Z9M`) and name the threat as overeager agentic harnesses that bypass the MCP's guards. A tool-layer gate is that kind of guard; a database role is not. The spec owner chose plain A on 2026-11-12, then adopted A2 on 2026-11-13 after checking the meeting recording.
76	
77	**Alternatives:** (A) the same session with the space account's full permissions and read-only only at the tool layer. It is about a week less work, but any process holding the bundle can write to the space. (B) a separate, permanently read-only agent principal with an `agent_reader` role and a grant table, the 2026-09-25 version of this decision. It revokes immediately, but the 2026-11-10 meeting judged its security gain marginal for about twice A2's extra work.
78	
79	### 5. Represent nodes as CrossApp nodes
80	
81	**Changed 2026-11-13: the node identifier is now the node's `rid`, not `Concept.id`, to match Sid's `shared-node-discovery` spec ([PR #1570](https://github.com/DiscourseGraphs/discourse-graph/pull/1570)), in which discovery returns each node as a `CrossAppNode`.** ENG-1985 and ENG-2091 implemented that on 2026-11-11: `dbNodesToCrossApp` in `packages/database/src/lib/dbToCrossAppConverters.ts` converts database rows to `DbCrossAppNode` (a `CrossAppNode` with `rid` and `modifiedAt` required), and discovery returns a `SharedNodeListing` of `{ nodes, spaces }`. Retrieval uses the same converter, so an agent and the plugins see the same node under the same ID.
82	
83	**IDs.** A node's ID is its `rid`: its space's URI followed by its `localId` (a Roam block uid, an Obsidian file's ID). A type's ID is the node's `nodeType`: the type's `localId` within the node's space, or the type's `rid` when it belongs to another space. Identically named types in different spaces stay separate. Look a node up by space and `localId`, never by `localId` alone.
84	
85	**Payload.** Return each node as a `DbCrossAppNode`, inside an envelope that follows discovery's `{ nodes, spaces }` pattern: the spaces map gives each node's space name, URI and platform, and type labels come from `dbNodeSchemasToCrossApp`. Search adds a score and an excerpt per node. Do not define a separate node type for agents.
86	
87	**Title and body.** The title is `content.direct`; `coreTitle` is the title without the type's format. The converter leaves out `content.full`, as discovery does, so get-node fetches the full Content separately, as node import does, and returns stored text/markdown, not rendered HTML. Preserve source links as text; do not fetch referenced assets or mint storage download URLs. Provenance comes from the `rid` and the spaces map. A source link refers to the origin and never claims the node exists in the caller's vault.
88	
89	**Gaps are errors.** `dbNodesToCrossApp` skips any row it cannot convert (missing direct content, author or node type) and logs a warning. Listings and search may skip such rows, as discovery does. Get-node for one ID must not: it converts the row with `dbNodeToCrossApp` and maps the failure to an explicit code, so a node that doesn't exist or isn't readable returns `not_found` and a node lacking its full Content returns `content_unavailable`. Distinguish a stored empty body from a missing row. Fixture validation must exercise these states for both platforms before release.
90	
91	**Type discovery** derives distinct types from readable node instances, independently of embeddings, with labels from the readable schemas. Missing schema data is a sync/access-integrity error, not a reason to bypass permissions.
92	
93	**Alternatives:** `Concept.id` serialized as a decimal string (the previous version of this decision) is a database-internal ID that no plugin uses; it would give the same node a second identity. An agent-specific node payload would rebuild, from the same rows, the second node representation that ENG-2091 just removed. Content IDs as node IDs would expose content variants as duplicate nodes.
94	
95	### 6. Reuse semantic vectors with a retrieval-specific query
96	
97	Embed each search query with `text-embedding-3-small` at 1536 dimensions to match the existing table. A local MCP has no server and no provider key, so it embeds through the existing website route `/api/embeddings/openai/small` and passes the vector to the search RPC. That route is unauthenticated today; see Risks. The API's search route embeds on the server after authenticating the caller. A caller-supplied vector cannot widen access, because the RPC ranks only nodes readable by the caller.
98	
99	Add a dedicated read-only search RPC using the existing embedding table and cosine-distance ordering. Keep existing RPC behavior for current consumers. In this query:
100	
101	- Resolve readable discourse node instances and any selected schema IDs.
102	- Join their current non-obsolete, usable embeddings for existing `direct` and `direct_and_description` content. Preserve the stored input semantics, including descriptions.
103	- Where multiple eligible embeddings represent one node, use its best similarity and return it once.
104	- Sort by similarity descending and node ID as a stable tie-breaker, then apply the requested limit. Authorization, type filtering, and deduplication occur before the limit.
105	
106	Do not copy the current threshold predicate or the Roam experiment's post-limit local filtering. Do not replace the threshold with zero, since negative similarities remain eligible. Do not add keyword indexes, hybrid fusion, or collection re-embedding.
107	
108	Nodes without a current usable embedding are absent from search but remain eligible for get-node/type discovery/context. Embedding-provider failures are errors, not empty results. Create excerpts from the first 300 Unicode code points of available synced body text, with a fallback to the stored semantic input when full content is absent; excerpts are not evidence that the query matched the body. Both interfaces document this behavior.
109	
110	**Alternative:** Calling the existing threshold RPC unchanged violates the agreed no-cutoff behavior and can lose results when type filtering follows its limit. A dedicated query reuses the existing search mechanism while preserving current consumers.
111	
112	### 7. Resolve discourse context using named roles
113	
114	Find readable materialized relation instances connected to the requested node, explicitly filtering `is_relation` and excluding schemas. Use `reference_content` source/destination roles to determine direction; the derived `refs` array identifies candidates but does not encode direction and can include other references. Require the relation, relationship type metadata, and both endpoints to be readable before returning a relationship summary.
115	
116	Return each relation ID with its type, direction, and connected-node summary. Preserve separate materialized relationships rather than deduplicating by labels. A self-link can produce both incoming and outgoing entries. Do not traverse beyond the requested node's incident relationships or expand ordinary backlinks.
117	
118	Return complete one-hop results within the host's response budget. If the result cannot fit, return an explicit `result_too_large` error rather than silently truncate or add an undocumented pagination contract. Full node bodies use the same complete-or-error policy. A proposed 1 MiB serialized response budget is an implementation guardrail to validate against Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex, not a relevance or latency target.
119	
120	**Alternative:** Expanding every ID in `refs` would expose non-discourse references and lose direction. Silent truncation would make incomplete discourse context appear complete.
121	
122	### 8. API contract and operational behavior
123	
124	Direct API routes and the corresponding MCP tools:
125	
126	| Direct API | MCP tool | Inputs |
127	| --- | --- | --- |
128	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}` | `get_node` | Node `rid` |
129	| `POST /api/v1/nodes/search` | `search_nodes` | Query, optional type IDs, optional limit |
130	| `GET /api/v1/node-types` | `get_node_types` | None |
131	| `GET /api/v1/nodes/{rid}/context` | `get_discourse_context` | Node `rid` |
132	
133	Node IDs are `rid`s (Decision 5). They contain `/` and `:`, so the API takes them URL-encoded in the path.
134	
135	Use shared Zod input/output schemas and generate or check the tool and API documentation against them. Reject blank queries, malformed `rid`s, empty explicitly supplied type filters, and non-integer/out-of-range limits with `invalid_request`. Omitted limits default to 10; valid limits are 1-30. Unknown but syntactically valid type IDs simply match no nodes. Results carry a request ID and `data` or an error object with a stable code and safe message.
136	
137	Missing, expired, or signed-out sessions fail authentication. Use the same `not_found` for nonexistent and unreadable nodes, `content_unavailable` for a readable node with missing required synced content, and `result_too_large` for response-budget failures; database and embedding failures are dependency errors. Return these as MCP tool errors with the same codes rather than serializing exceptions; the API maps them to 401, 404, 409, 422 and 503. Do not turn failed queries into successful empty collections.
138	
139	Keep diagnostic logs to request ID, operation, duration, result count, and error category. Exclude the bundle, refresh and access tokens, query text, node bodies, and provider payloads. A local MCP's logs stay on the user's machine. The API's redaction covers the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs as well as application logs. No read-history UI or auditing subsystem is added. Documentation includes the install and setup flow, private bundle handling, search coverage/limits, sync-gap errors, and source-link limitations.
140	
141	## Risks / Trade-offs
142	
143	- [Revocation waits for token expiry] → Accepted under A2 (Decision 4). A signed-out session keeps its current access token for up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
144	- [The access token hook runs on every sign-in] → A failing hook blocks every token, including the plugins'. Keep it to one indexed lookup in `mcp_session`, return claims unchanged for other sessions, and test plugin sign-in and refresh with the hook enabled.
145	- [A read grant missing from `mcp_reader` breaks retrieval silently] → Retrieval fails or returns fewer rows when the role lacks a grant or a `TO authenticated` policy excludes it. Cucumber scenarios run every operation as `mcp_reader`, not as `authenticated`.
146	- [The bundle reads everything the space can read, from a plain file the agent harness can read] → Agent clients keep MCP configuration in plain files on the user's machine (for example `claude_desktop_config.json`, or `~/.claude.json` for Claude Code). Accepted for v0. Setup documentation states the risk.
147	- [The API carries a bearer token through the website] → An MCP session's token is read-only. A plugin session's token can write, but the API exposes only reads and never stores the token. Redaction covers the `Authorization` header in hosting and proxy logs as well as application logs. A token that leaks stays valid until it expires, up to `jwt_expiry` (3600 s).
148	- [Cutting off one MCP depends on `mcp-session-access` sign-out] → If per-session sign-out is not in v0 (open there as task 0.4), the only cut-off is changing the space password, which signs out every plugin instance of the space.
149	- [The query embedding route is unauthenticated] → MCP search depends on it, and today anyone can spend the team's OpenAI quota through it, independent of this change. API search embeds on the server behind authentication instead. Hardening it is a follow-up, not this change: the shipped Roam and Obsidian plugins call the route without auth during sync and search, and installed copies cannot be force-updated, so a check needs a compatible migration path.
150	- [Installed MCP copies pin the RPC signatures] → Copies on users' machines cannot be force-updated. Add RPC versions alongside old ones rather than changing signatures in place.
151	- [One bundle reads one space] → A user with several spaces needs one MCP entry per space. Whether one agent should span several spaces is an open product question.
152	- [Existing embedding inputs differ across platforms] → Preserve and document that behavior, use deterministic vector fixtures for query correctness, and defer relevance tuning until real-query examples exist.
153	- [Full content, schema metadata, or provenance can be missing] → Return explicit sync/data errors and validate representative Roam and Obsidian fixtures. Do not expand ingestion or attachment scope to conceal gaps.
154	- [Shared nodes surprise users or origin links do not open locally] → Explain that results reflect readable synced data rather than local import membership and label provenance as origin.
155	- [Large bodies/context exceed client budgets] → Validate the response budget and surface a complete-or-error result. Pagination or truncation semantics require a later product decision.
156	
157	## Migration Plan
158	
159	1. Land `mcp-session-access` first: the session registry, the handoff helper, and the plugin connect command. This change depends on it. Then add `mcp_reader` and the access token hook (Decision 4), and enable the hook on the hosted project.
160	2. Add the narrow retrieval RPCs — node fetch, search without a relevance threshold, type discovery, and one-hop context — through the database's declarative schema/migration workflow. Existing clients and search RPCs retain their behavior.
161	3. Build the local MCP with the four tools over those RPCs and the embedding route, and the direct API routes in `apps/website` over the same RPCs.
162	4. Test permission gains/losses, both platform payloads, shared unimported nodes, type filters, negative similarities, missing embeddings/content, inaccessible relation endpoints, and parity between the MCP and the direct API. Assert that the database refuses writes made with a handed-over session and still accepts the plugin's. Install the MCP in Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex with a test space's bundle, record client versions, and demonstrate all four operations with Roam and Obsidian closed. Run required repository validation before requesting implementation review.
163	5. Release the MCP to a limited validation cohort, then expand only after those checks pass. No bulk content migration or re-embedding is part of rollout.
164	6. Rollback withdraws the MCP package and signs out registered MCP sessions; without per-session sign-out, change the space password. Additive retrieval RPCs can remain unused; do not delete synced nodes, content, vectors, or existing group access.
165	
166	## Open Questions
167	
168	The credential label copy, example queries for documentation, and a future relevance evaluation dataset can be settled during implementation without changing this architecture.
169	
170	### Per-capability open decisions
171	
172	<!-- Held here rather than in the spec deltas: openspec validate warns that a
173	     "## Open decisions" section in a delta is not carried into the main spec on archive. -->
174	
175	- **`agent-read-access`:** The per-space model stands as the v0 baseline after the 2026-11-10 decision. Whether one agent should span several spaces is open.
176	- **`discourse-mcp`:** The client set is Claude Desktop, Claude Code and Codex. ChatGPT cannot launch a local MCP and is out of v0.
177	- **`discourse-retrieval`:** Implementation design for access/type filtering, limits, excerpts, errors, and missing embeddings is above. Real-query relevance examples and numerical quality targets are deferred. Hybrid search is future work.

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Let a space hand an agent its own session for the space account, so the agent reads the space's synced discourse graph with the space's current access.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Session handoff from the plugin

An agent SHALL obtain its credential through the `mcp-session-access` handoff: a Roam or Obsidian plugin signed in as the space account opens a new session and shows the user a bundle once. No website session or agent-management page SHALL be required.

#### Scenario: Setup from either supported platform

- **WHEN** a user runs the connect command in an authenticated Roam or Obsidian client
- **THEN** the plugin shows a bundle for a new session of that client's space account
- **AND** the plugin's own session is unchanged

### Requirement: Per-space principal

The system SHALL treat the space account whose session was handed over as the principal. Retrieval SHALL use that account's readable collection and SHALL NOT combine the access of other space accounts used by the same human. Reading another space's synced but unpublished nodes SHALL require a bundle from that space.

#### Scenario: Another space's private synced nodes

- **GIVEN** a human uses spaces A and B and a node in B is not readable by A's space account
- **WHEN** an agent uses a bundle from space A
- **THEN** it cannot retrieve the node in B
- **AND** access through B requires a bundle from space B

#### Scenario: Accessible shared node

- **GIVEN** a node from another space is readable by the space account through sharing
- **WHEN** the agent retrieves that node
- **THEN** the node is eligible without requiring local import or authorship by the space account

### Requirement: Current permissions and revocation

The system SHALL evaluate retrieval against the space account's current read permissions. Removing access SHALL stop subsequent retrieval of affected data, and adding access SHALL make affected synced data eligible, without a new bundle. Signing out a handed-over session SHALL stop it from refreshing; access tokens it already holds MAY remain valid until they expire.

#### Scenario: Permissions change after handoff

- **WHEN** a space account gains access to node A and loses access to node B after a bundle is handed over
- **THEN** subsequent requests with that bundle can retrieve A and cannot retrieve B
- **AND** a new bundle is not required

#### Scenario: Session sign-out

- **WHEN** a user signs out a handed-over session
- **THEN** the MCP cannot refresh that session
- **AND** requests fail once its current access token expires

### Requirement: The database enforces read-only on handed-over sessions

The database SHALL refuse any create, modify or delete made with a handed-over session, including calls to sync, upsert and session-management functions, whichever client makes them. The session SHALL keep the space account's read access. The plugin's own sessions SHALL keep their permissions. The MCP SHALL expose only retrieval tools, and the direct API SHALL expose only retrieval operations. Missing, expired or signed-out sessions SHALL NOT authorize retrieval.

#### Scenario: Agent asks the MCP to modify a node

- **GIVEN** the space account can edit a node
- **WHEN** an agent asks the MCP to modify that node
- **THEN** no MCP tool can perform the modification
- **AND** the node remains unchanged

#### Scenario: Write made outside the MCP's tools

- **GIVEN** a process holds the handed-over session and the space account can edit a node
- **WHEN** it modifies the node by calling the database directly with that session
- **THEN** the database refuses the modification
- **AND** the node remains unchanged

#### Scenario: Plugin session keeps write access

- **GIVEN** a plugin has handed over a session
- **WHEN** the plugin writes with its own session
- **THEN** the write succeeds

#### Scenario: Unauthenticated retrieval

- **WHEN** a retrieval request has a missing, expired or signed-out session
- **THEN** no discourse data is returned
=== discourse-mcp/spec.md
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Expose headless discourse retrieval to agent clients through one platform-independent local MCP, run on the user's machine with a space account session handed over by the plugin.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Four retrieval tools

MCP SHALL expose tools for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types, and get-discourse-context. Tool descriptions and input definitions SHALL make the operations and supported search/type-filter inputs discoverable. The tools SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` and `agent-read-access` contracts.

#### Scenario: Tool discovery and invocation

- **WHEN** an authenticated agent client discovers the MCP tools
- **THEN** all four operations and their input definitions are available
- **AND** invoking them applies the agreed payloads, access rules, search limits, and discourse-context boundaries

### Requirement: Direct API and MCP parity

MCP SHALL accept the same handed-over session as the direct API and SHALL expose equivalent retrieval semantics. A caller SHALL NOT gain access to additional data by switching interfaces.

#### Scenario: Equivalent requests through both interfaces

- **GIVEN** unchanged data and permissions and a valid handed-over session
- **WHEN** equivalent requests are made through MCP and the direct API
- **THEN** they apply equivalent eligibility, payload, filtering, ranking, and limit rules

#### Scenario: Signed-out session across interfaces

- **WHEN** a session previously used successfully with both interfaces is signed out
- **THEN** once its current access token expires, subsequent requests through both interfaces are denied

### Requirement: Supported agent clients

V0 SHALL support documented installation and setup of the local MCP, and successful execution of all four operations, in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex. ChatGPT is not supported in v0, because it cannot launch a local MCP. This capability SHALL require no separate platform-specific MCP for Roam versus Obsidian.

#### Scenario: Validate each target client

- **GIVEN** synced readable data and a bundle created through the supported handoff
- **WHEN** installation, setup and tool execution are validated independently in Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and Codex
- **THEN** each client can launch the MCP and complete all four retrieval operations
- **AND** retrieval works with Roam and Obsidian closed
=== discourse-retrieval/spec.md
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Let agents retrieve synced discourse node text, search by meaning using existing embeddings, discover usable node types, and follow explicit one-hop discourse context within current read access.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Readable synced collection <!-- roam:RfGa1ASkz -->

All retrieval operations SHALL use already-synced discourse data readable by the handed-over space account. Local import status and authorship SHALL NOT restrict that collection. Results MUST NOT imply that returned nodes have been imported into the client application.

#### Scenario: Readable but unimported node

- **GIVEN** a synced discourse node is readable by the principal but was authored elsewhere and never imported into its client
- **WHEN** the agent fetches it or searches for it
- **THEN** the node is eligible for retrieval and search ranking
- **AND** the response does not assert local import membership

#### Scenario: Unreadable node

- **WHEN** an agent requests a node that its principal cannot read
- **THEN** retrieval does not return the node's content or metadata

### Requirement: Full node text <!-- roam:M6O5NmufQ -->

Getting a readable node SHALL return its ID, title, type, full synced text body, and source/provenance link. The body SHALL reflect stored synced text, without fetching current content from the client application. Attachment downloads and image/file contents SHALL remain outside this operation.

#### Scenario: Get a node with body text and attachment links

- **WHEN** an agent fetches a readable synced node containing text and a link to an attachment
- **THEN** it receives the required node fields and full stored text, including source links present in that text
- **AND** the response does not download or embed the attachment's file contents

### Requirement: Existing semantic search <!-- roam:Mcp8fO0Ya -->

Search SHALL reuse the existing semantic search functionality and stored embeddings, including Roam's title-plus-description embeddings. Search SHALL NOT require re-embedding the collection as titles only. Matching SHALL reflect the existing embedding inputs rather than promise full-body coverage. V0 SHALL NOT require keyword matching or hybrid ranking. Each result SHALL contain node ID, title, type, a short excerpt, and source/provenance link, ordered by relevance.

#### Scenario: Semantic search results

- **WHEN** an agent submits a query with eligible nodes that have current searchable embeddings
- **THEN** results are ranked by semantic similarity using those embeddings and include the required result fields
- **AND** a node is not excluded solely because its title lacks the query's exact words

#### Scenario: Existing title-plus-description embedding

- **GIVEN** a readable Roam node has an existing embedding generated from its title and description
- **WHEN** the agent searches
- **THEN** that embedding contributes to ranking without being replaced by a title-only embedding

#### Scenario: Unembedded body changes

- **GIVEN** stored searchable embeddings, permissions, and filters remain unchanged
- **WHEN** only a node's full synced body changes
- **THEN** that change does not directly alter its semantic matching score

### Requirement: Bounded search without a relevance cutoff <!-- roam:C7DJ2nVgj -->

Search SHALL default to 10 results and return at most 30 results per request. A supported requested limit between 1 and 30 SHALL bound the response. V0 SHALL offer no pagination and SHALL NOT discard eligible searchable nodes solely because their relevance is low. An empty collection SHALL mean there are no eligible searchable nodes under the access and type constraints, not that a relevance threshold was unmet.

#### Scenario: Default and explicit limits

- **GIVEN** at least 30 eligible searchable nodes
- **WHEN** the agent searches without a limit or with a supported limit of 20
- **THEN** the respective responses contain 10 or 20 results
- **AND** neither response offers a continuation page

#### Scenario: Weak matches

- **GIVEN** three eligible searchable nodes with weak semantic similarity and a requested limit of 10
- **WHEN** the agent searches
- **THEN** all three are returned in relevance order without rejection by a relevance cutoff

#### Scenario: Empty eligible collection

- **WHEN** no searchable nodes satisfy the principal's access and requested type constraints
- **THEN** search returns an empty result collection

#### Scenario: Requested limit exceeds the maximum

- **WHEN** a request specifies a limit above 30
- **THEN** the service does not return more than 30 results

### Requirement: Readable type discovery and filtering <!-- roam:xtDHC9uuv -->

Type discovery SHALL expose type IDs and names only for types present on nodes the principal can currently read, including accessible shared nodes. Search SHALL accept one or more type IDs with OR semantics. Omitting the filter SHALL search across all eligible types.

#### Scenario: Discover types from readable nodes

- **GIVEN** type A is present on a readable shared node and type B occurs only on unreadable nodes
- **WHEN** the agent discovers node types
- **THEN** type A is available and type B is absent

#### Scenario: Multiple selected types

- **WHEN** the agent searches with types A and B selected
- **THEN** every result has type A or B and is readable by the principal

#### Scenario: No type filter

- **WHEN** the agent searches without a type filter
- **THEN** no eligible node is excluded based on type

### Requirement: One-hop discourse context <!-- roam:IffvWYML9 -->

Discourse context SHALL return incoming and outgoing explicit discourse relationships for a readable node. Each returned relationship SHALL identify its type and direction relative to the requested node and the connected node's ID, title, and type. Both endpoints MUST be readable. Ordinary backlinks SHALL be excluded, and connected bodies SHALL be separately retrievable through get-node. A single call SHALL NOT perform arbitrary-depth traversal.

#### Scenario: Incoming and outgoing relationships

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A and B have an explicit relationship from A to B
- **WHEN** the agent requests discourse context for A and then for B
- **THEN** the relationship is outgoing for A and incoming for B, with the corresponding connected-node summary

#### Scenario: Inaccessible endpoint and ordinary backlink

- **GIVEN** readable node A has an explicit relationship to unreadable node B and an ordinary backlink from readable node C
- **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** neither the relationship to B nor the ordinary backlink from C is returned

#### Scenario: Repeated one-hop calls

- **GIVEN** readable nodes A, B, and C have explicit relationships A to B and B to C, with no A to C relationship
- **WHEN** the agent requests A's discourse context
- **THEN** that call does not traverse B to return C
- **AND** a subsequent request for B's discourse context can retrieve the relationship to C

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Give developers a documented interface for direct discourse retrieval using the same space account session and behavioral contracts as MCP.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Direct access to retrieval operations <!-- roam:9iZVchr-f -->

The system SHALL provide a directly callable API for get-node, search-nodes, discover-node-types, and get-discourse-context. These operations SHALL follow the `discourse-retrieval` and `agent-read-access` contracts without requiring an MCP client.

#### Scenario: Developer calls each operation directly

- **WHEN** a developer uses a valid handed-over session to call each of the four API operations
- **THEN** each operation is available directly and applies the shared retrieval and authorization rules
- **AND** an MCP connection is not required

### Requirement: Documented developer contract <!-- roam:OlfosIASW -->

The API SHALL document authentication, operation inputs and outputs, errors, search limits, type-filter semantics, and the per-space access model. Documentation SHALL explain that readable unimported nodes can appear, existing embeddings determine semantic coverage, semantic search can return weak matches, and v0 search has no pagination.

#### Scenario: Set up a direct integration

- **WHEN** a developer follows the API documentation using a handed-over session
- **THEN** the documentation supplies callable examples for all four operations and explains how to interpret their results and errors

### Requirement: Headless retrieval after setup <!-- roam:UCHDnQtCv -->

After session handoff and data sync, direct retrieval SHALL work without Roam or Obsidian being open. Responses SHALL use the database's synced state rather than require a live connection to either client application.

#### Scenario: Source client is closed

- **GIVEN** a user has synced nodes and a handed-over session
- **WHEN** the source application is closed and the developer calls the retrieval API
- **THEN** eligible synced data remains retrievable
